safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) آتيناه; (حكما) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) is parenthetical; (كذلك) is attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is نجزي.
The clause «بلغ ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) ... and the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «استوى ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause بلغ أشدّه.
The clause «آتيناه ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «نجزي ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
(15) (الواو) is a conjunction; (على حين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of دخل; (من أهلها) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of غفلة; (فيها) is attached to (وجد); (من شيعته) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هذا, and likewise (من عدوّه); (الفاء) is a conjunction; the second (من شيعته) is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative الذي; (على الذي) is attached to (استغاثه) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the sense of استنصره; the second (من عدوّه) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the second relative الذي; (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places; (عليه) is attached to (قضى); (من عمل) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هذا; (مضلّ) is a second khabar; (مبين) is a naʿt of مضلّ ...
The clause «دخل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «وجد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause دخل.
The clause «يقتتلان ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of رجلين.
The clause «هذا من شيعته» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of يقتتلان [Note: Or it has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «هذا من عدوّه» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause هذا من شيعته.
The clause «استغاثة ...» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic verb is استغاثه.] has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause وجد.
The clause «وكزه موسى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استغاثة ...
The clause «قضى عليه.» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause وكزه موسى.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «هذا من عمل ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّه عدوّ ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) - or an explanatory resumption.-

* Morphology:
(استغاث) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its origin is استغيث: the fatḥa of the yāʾ was transferred to the ghayn, then the yāʾ was converted into an alif.

* Benefits:
- إِنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ مُضِلٌّ مُبِينٌ:
We have previously dealt with the multiplicity of the khabar and its repetition. We remind the reader of what we said:
The khabar is not multiple if the multiplicity conveys a shared attribute, as when we say: "So-and-so is tall short", i.e. he is "of medium build" or "of average height", so in this case we do not speak of "multiplicity of the khabar". Among instances of multiplicity is His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ مُضِلٌّ مُبِينٌ.
- The continuation of the story of Moses and Pharaoh:
Pharaoh adopted Moses, and he became the son of Pharaoh. They sought wet-nurses for him, but he turned away from all their breasts. His sister was following his trail, and when she saw his refusal to suckle she offered to bring them a woman who would nurse him, and she brought them his mother. She gave him her breast and he began to suckle it, and his mother nearly revealed to them his affair and hers, «لَوْلا أَنْ رَبَطْنا عَلى قَلْبِها».
After a while Āsiya presented him to Pharaoh, and Moses began plucking at his beard. That alarmed Pharaoh, and he called for the slaughterers to slaughter him. Pharaoh's wife kept pleading with her husband for compassion; she placed before him a fruit and a live coal, and he stretched out his hand to the coal, took it and put it in his mouth, and it burned him. By that Pharaoh realized his lack of discernment and pardoned him. When he became a youth he used to ride with Pharaoh and go with him wherever he went. Moses learned that Pharaoh had ridden to a town, so he followed him there, and it had been emptied for him. He saw an Israelite and a Copt fighting each other; the Israelite called on him for help, so Moses struck the Copt with his fist and finished him off. Moses regretted his deed and said: This is of the work of Satan, «إِنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ مُضِلٌّ مُبِينٌ» ...
The story has a continuation which we shall come to in the coming āyas, Allah willing.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) is a muḍāf (genitive construct) munādā (one addressed), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ that was deleted for lightening, and the deleted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, and the second is a conjunction; (لي) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اغفر); (له) is attached to (غفر); (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun in (إنّه), in the position of the accusative by way of borrowing (istiʿāra).]; (الرحيم) is a second khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّي ظلمت ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ظلمت ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «اغفر ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If I am guilty by this, then forgive."
The clause «غفر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّه هو الغفور ...» has no grammatical position: a causal resumption.
The clause «هو الغفور ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ ...

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(قال ربّ) is like the previous one [Note: in āya (16).]; (الباء) is causal; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e.: أنعمته عليّ.]; (عليّ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنعمت).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما أنعمت ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اعصمني" ... and in it there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "By the right of Your favouring me with forgiveness, protect me" ...
(الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (للمجرمين) is attached to (ظهيرا).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech) [Note: It is permissible for the vocative clause to be parenthetical, for supplication, with no grammatical position, and the clause (اعصمني) بما أنعمت ... is the maqūl al-qawl.].
The clause (اعصمني) بما أنعمت ... has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لن أكون ظهيرا ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If You protect me, then I will never be ..."

safi-cedvel:18-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (في المدينة) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) (خائفا), and the noun of أصبح is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Moses; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (إذا) is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (بالأمس) is attached to (استنصره); (له) is attached to (قال); (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
The clause «أصبح ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يترقّب ...» is in the position of the accusative as a second khabar of (أصبح) [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in (خائفا), and it may be a badal (substitute) of (خائفا).].
The clause «الذي استنصره ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أصبح.
The clause «استنصره ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «يستصرخه ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الذي).
The clause «قال له موسى ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّك لغويّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
(19) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) قال; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (بالذي) is attached to (يبطش); (لهما) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of عدوّ [Note: Or attached to (عدو) in the sense of معاد (hostile).] ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يبطش) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being أراد.
The agent of (قال) is a latent pronoun referring to the one of his own party [Note: Some grammarians said that the pronoun refers to the Copt, imagining that he [Translator's note: i.e. the Copt] was the killer of the man of the previous day.]; (موسى) is a singular proper-noun munādā (one addressed), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (أن تقتلني) is like أن يبطش; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (بالأمس) is attached to (قتلت).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقتلني ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تريد ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قتلت ...) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is تقتلني.
(إن) is negative; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن تكون) is like أن يبطش; (في الأرض) is attached to (جبّارا), the khabar.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تريد, and likewise the interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون من المصلحين) is the object of the second تريد, and (ما) is negative ...
The clause «أراد ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يبطش ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «هو عدوّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «تريد» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «تقتلني ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قتلت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «إن تريد» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «تكون جبارا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ما تريد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إن تريد ...

* Morphology:
(غويّ) is an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral غوى يغوي, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فعيل; the yāʾ of فعيل was assimilated (idghām) into the lām (third radical) of the word, which is the yāʾ.

* Benefits:
- The redundancy of «أن»:
«أن» is regularly redundant (zāʾida) after the temporal «لمّا», and before «لو» when preceded by an oath, as in the poet's saying:
فأقسم أن لو التقينا وأنتم ... لكان لكم يوم من الشر مظلم
(I swear that had we and you met, you would have had a day of evil, dark.)
Like that is His saying, Glorified is He: «فَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَ الْبَشِيرُ أَلْقاهُ عَلى وَجْهِهِ». The presence of «أن» points to slowness and lack of haste.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من أقصى) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاء); (بك) is attached to (يأتمرون); (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (يقتلوك) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يقتلوك..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يأتمرون).
(الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (لك) is attached to الناصحين; (من الناصحين) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «جاء رجل..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسعى ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رجل.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive..
The clause «يا موسى إنّ الملأ ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّ الملأ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «يأتمرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ ...
The clause «يقتلوك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «اخرج ...» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "If you want safety, then go out."
The clause «إنّي لك من الناصحين ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...
(21) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (منها) is attached to (خرج); (خائفا) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of خرج; (قال ربّ): its i'rab has been given [Note: in āya (16) of this sūra.].
(النون) in (نجّني) is for protection (wiqāya); (من القوم) is attached to (نجّني) ...
The clause «خرج ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال.
The clause «يترقّب ...» is in the position of the accusative as a second ḥāl [Note: See āya (18) of this sūra.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ...
The clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, for seeking mercy.
The clause «نجّني ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.

* Morphology:
(أقصى) is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral قصا يقصو, of the class of نصر; its pattern is أفعل, and it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion) because the letter before the wāw has a fatḥa.

safi-cedvel:22-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) قال; (تلقاء) is an accusative adverb of place attached to (توجّه); (مدين) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine; (عسى) is a defective past verb - an abrogator (nāsikh) -; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, and the nūn in (يهديني) is for protection (wiqāya); (سواء) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يهديني ...) is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of عسى.
The clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis ... has no grammatical position: resumptive..
The clause «توجّه ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «عسى ربّي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «يهديني ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
(23) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لمّا ورد.. وجد) is like لمّا توجّه ... قال; (عليه) is attached to (وجد); (من الناس) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أمّة; (من دونهم) is attached to (وجد) [Note: It is transitive to one object in both places, in the sense of لقي (to meet).]; (ما) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being (خطبكما); (لا) is negative; (حتّى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive; (يصدر) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى; (الواو) is a conjunction ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يصدر) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to (نسقي).
The clause «ورد ماء ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «وجد ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يسقون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of أمّة [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أمّة, because it is described.].
The clause «وجد (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause وجد (the first).
The clause «تذودان ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of امرأتين.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ما خطبكما ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «قالتا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا نسقي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يصدر الرعاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أبونا شيخ ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لا نسقي.
(24) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لهما) is attached to (سقى); (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (إلى الظلّ) is attached to (تولّى); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (قال ربّ): its i'rab has been given [Note: in āya (16) of this sūra.]; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to فقير by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the sense of محتاج (in need), and the returning pronoun is omitted; (إليّ) is attached to (أنزلت); (من خير) is attached to a ḥāl of the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. أنزلته من خير [Note: Or it is a tamyīz (specification) of the relative (ما).]; (فقير) is the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «سقى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قالتا ...
The clause «تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause سقى ...
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تولّى.
The vocative clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, for seeking mercy.
The clause «إنّي ... فقير ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أنزلت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(25) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (على استحياء) is a ḥāl of the agent of تمشي; (اللام) is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يجزيك) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (لنا) is attached to (سقيت) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجزيك) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يدعوك).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما سقيت ...) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا جاءه ... قال) is like لمّا توجّه ... قال; (عليه) is attached to (قصّ); (لا) is the jussive-governing particle of prohibition; (من القوم) is attached to (نجوت) ...
The clause «جاءته إحداهما ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "So they returned and told their father ... and he said to one of them: Call him ... so she came to him ..."
The clause «تمش ...» [Translator's note: so in the source, for تمشي.] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of جاءته.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ أبي يدعوك ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يدعوك ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يجزيك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «سقيت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «جاءه ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قصّ ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause جاءه.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لا تخف ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «نجوت ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...

* Morphology:
(23) يسقون: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يسقيون - with a yāʾ bearing ḍamma before the wāw -. The ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made vowelless and the vowel was transferred to the qāf - iʿlāl by making vowelless -; two vowelless letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw, so the yāʾ was deleted and it became يسقون; its pattern is يفعون.
(الرعاء) is the plural of راع, an active participle from the triliteral رعى. It [Translator's note: i.e. راع] contains iʿlāl by deletion on account of the tanwīn - the meeting of two vowelless letters -; its pattern is فاع. In رعاء there is ibdāl (substitution) of the yāʾ by a hamza; its origin is الرعاي, and since the yāʾ came at the end after a vowelless alif, it was converted into a hamza. The pattern of الرعاء is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ [Note: al-Zamakhsharī made this plural regular (qiyāsī), like صيام and قيام; some said it is a plural formed irregularly, for the regular plural of the manqūṣ noun weak in its lām is فعلة, as in قضاة and رماة, with ḍamma on the first letter and two fatḥas.].
(25) استحياء: a regular maṣdar of the six-letter verb استحيى; its pattern is استفعال ... It contains ibdāl of the lām of the maṣdar - which is the yāʾ - by a hamza, because it came at the end after a vowelless alif; its origin is استحياي.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, وَأَبُونا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ:
They wanted to say to him: We are two weak, modest women; we are unable to jostle with the men, we have no man to undertake that, and our father is an old man advanced in age, whom old age has weakened and exhausted, so we must delay the watering until the people have finished their business with the water.
Allusion (al-ishāra): in His saying, the Exalted, عَلَى اسْتِحْياءٍ:
With a swift glance, like the glance of an eye, and in a language that is the language of looking, He alluded to the description of her splendid, captivating beauty by "shyness", because bashfulness is among the attributes of beautiful women, and because a graceful, swaying gait is among their most prominent features.

* Benefits:
1- إحدى:
The numbers one and two agree with the counted noun: they are masculine with the masculine and feminine with the feminine. But there is a difference between the two numbers: "one" is made feminine by the presence of the shortened alif, «احدى», and masculine by deleting this alif, which is written as a yāʾ: «أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً». As for «الاثنان», its feminine is by attaching the tāʾ, «اثنتان», and its masculine by deleting the tāʾ, «اثنان»; and like the former in the feminine is «ثنتان», with the alif deleted from its beginning.
2- The word «خير»:
«خير» occurs as a plain noun applied to every good thing, the opposite of «الشر» (evil), as in this āya: «رَبِّ إِنِّي لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ». It also occurs as an elative noun (ism tafḍīl), as in His speech, the Exalted, on the tongue of Iblīs: «أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ», i.e. better than him.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(أبت) is a muḍāf (genitive construct) munādā (one addressed), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, and the kasra - the kasra of harmony - was transferred to the tāʾ substituted for the yāʾ of the speaker ... and (التاء) is a compensation for the deleted yāʾ of the speaker, and the deleted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. استأجرته; (الأمين) is a second khabar (predicate) of (إن) [Translator's note: so in the source, for إنّ].
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يا أبت استأجره ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «استأجره ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ خير ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya)..
The clause «استأجرت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

* Rhetoric:
Comprehensive, conclusive speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): in His saying, the Exalted: إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ.
It is wise, comprehensive speech to which nothing can be added, because when these two qualities, I mean strength and trustworthiness, are combined in the one who manages your affair, your mind is set at rest and your purpose is fulfilled. By sending forth this speech, whose course is the course of a proverb, the need was dispensed with - and this is the wisdom - of saying: "Hire him for his strength and his trustworthiness."

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (أنكحك) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); (إحدى) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; (هاتين) is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of ابنتيّ, indeclinable (mabnī) on the yāʾ, in the position of the genitive [Note: There is disagreement among the grammarians over whether the dual demonstrative is indeclinable or declinable; the prevailing view is that it is indeclinable.]; (أن) is like the first; (ثماني) is an accusative adverb of time, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأجرني), and the object of تأجرني is omitted, i.e.: تأجرني نفسك (you hire yourself out to me) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أنكحك ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أريد.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأجرني ...) is in the position of the genitive by (على), attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of أنكحك or of its object, i.e. مستأجرا - with kasra on the jīm - or مستأجرا - with fatḥa on it -.
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (أتممت) is a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (عشرا) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (أتممت) [Note: The tamyīz (specification) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. عشر حجج (ten years).]; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (من عندك) is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: التمام من عندك (the completion is from you); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (أن أشقّ) is like أن أنكحك; (عليك) is attached to (أشقّ) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أشقّ ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أريد.
(السين) is a particle of the future, and (النون) in (تجدني) is for protection (wiqāya); (شاء) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; (من الصالحين) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is تجدني ...
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّي أريد ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أريد ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «أنكحك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تأجرني ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أتممت ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «(التمام) من عندك ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما أريد ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أتممت.
The clause «أشقّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ستجدني ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «إن شاء الله ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

* Morphology:
(حجج) is the plural of حجّة, a noun for the year; its pattern [Translator's note: i.e. that of the singular حجّة] is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(بيني) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ذلك [Note: i.e. that condition stands between me and you.]; (بينك) is like بيني and conjoined to it; (أيّما) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) ... and ما is redundant (zāʾida); (قضيت) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (عدوان) is the noun of لا, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (عليّ) is attached to the omitted khabar of لا; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive ... and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. نقوله.] ...
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما نقول ...) is in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar وكيل.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ذلك بيني ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «قضيت ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «لا عدوان عليّ ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «الله ... وكيل» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قضيت.
The clause «نقول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).

* Benefits:
1- أيّما الأجلين:
This «أي» occurs in five ways:
a- It is conditional, as in «أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ», and the «ما» attached to it is redundant, for emphasis.
b- It is interrogative: «أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً».
c- It is relative: «مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ».
d- It indicates the sense of perfection, and is an adjective of an indefinite noun, as in «عليّ رجل أيّ رجل» (ʿAlī is a man, what a man!), i.e. complete in the qualities of men; it is also a ḥāl (circumstantial) after a definite noun, as in «مررت بعبد الله أيّ رجل» (I passed by ʿAbd Allāh, what a man!).
e- It is a link for addressing in the vocative what has «أل», as in «يا أيّها الرجل».

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) آنس; (بأهله) is attached to (سار), and (الباء) is for accompaniment; (من جانب) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (نارا) [Note: attached to (آنس).]; (لأهله) is attached to (قال); (آتيكم) is the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ, nominative (marfūʿ) [Note: It may be an active participle from أتى, or the imperfect (آتي).], and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (منها) is attached to (آتيكم) [Note: It may be attached to a ḥāl of خبر.]; (بخبر) is attached to (آتيكم); (جذوة) is conjoined to خبر by the conjunction, or genitive; (من النار) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of جذوة ...
The clause «سار ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause قضى ...
The clause «آنس ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «امكثوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّي آنست ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) - or an explanatory resumption - and the clause «آنست ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لعليّ آتيكم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: It may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of آنست, i.e. hoping to bring news ... This is if a ḥāl may validly come as a performative (inshāʾī) clause.].
The clause «لعلّكم تصطلون ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption.
The clause «تصطلون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لعلّ ...

* Morphology:
(سار) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its origin is سير: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted into an alif; its pattern is فعل.
(خبر) is a noun for what is transmitted of talk and other things; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(جذوة) is a noun for the stick at whose head there is fire, or for a stick in general; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn - the fāʾ may take any of the three vowels -.

safi-cedvel:30-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا أتاها) is like لمّا قضى ... «1»,
(من شاطئ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نودي), and likewise (في البقعة); (من الشجرة) is a badal (substitute) of الشاطئ, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), with repetition of the preposition; (أن) is a particle of explanation (tafsīr); (موسى) is a singular proper-noun munādā (one addressed), indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, in the position of the accusative; (أنا) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun in (إني), borrowed for the accusative position.]; (ربّ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty, nominative (marfūʿ).
The clause «أتاها ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «نودي ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يا موسى ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «إنّي أنا الله ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «أنا الله ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(31) (الواو) is a conjunction; (أن) is like the first; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا رآها ...) is like لمّا قضى «3»; (مدبرا) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial); (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (يا موسى) is like the first; (لا) is the jussive-governing particle of prohibition; (من الآمنين) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ألق ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «رآها ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تهتزّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the object of رآها.
The clause «كأنّها جانّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of تهتزّ.
The clause «ولّى ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لم يعقّب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
The second vocative clause has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أقبل ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تخف ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أقبل.
The clause «إنّك من الآمنين ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...
(32) (في جيبك) is attached to (اسلك); (تخرج) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the command; (بيضاء) is an accusative ḥāl of the agent of تخرج; (من غير ...) is attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in بيضاء; (إليك) is attached to (اضمم); (من الرهب) is attached to (اضمم), i.e. on account of it; (الفاء) is resumptive; (ذانك) is a demonstrative, indeclinable on the alif, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being برهانان; (من ربّك) is attached to a naʿt of the khabar; (إلى فرعون) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذهب" [Note: Or to an omitted second naʿt of (برهانان), its implied form being مرسلان (sent).] ...
The clause «اسلك ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: Or a badal of the clause أقبل.].
The clause «تخرج ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e.: "If you insert your hand, it will come out ..."
The clause «اضمم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اسلك.
The clause «ذانك برهانان ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption in the context of the call.
The clause «إنّهم كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «كانوا قوما ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(شاطئ) is a noun for the land adjoining the sea, on the pattern فاعل, and it is originally the valley [Translator's note: so in the source].
(الأيمن): a derived adjective on the pattern أفعل; it is the side adjoining the right of a person, and it may be from اليمن, i.e. blessing; superiority (tafḍīl) is not intended by it.
(البقعة) is a noun for the part of the ground on which a person stands; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(32) (ذانك) is a demonstrative for the dual, indeclinable on the alif according to the more likely view - and some make it declinable by letters.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (al-takrīr): in His saying, the Exalted: اسْلُكْ يَدَكَ فِي جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ. He repeated the one meaning because of the difference of the two purposes: the purpose in one of them is the hand's coming out white, and in the second the concealment of fear.
Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ.
Drawing in the wing is a metonymy for fortitude and self-control. It is taken from the action of a bird when safe after fear; it is originally borrowed from the action of the bird in this state, then its use became frequent for fortitude and self-control, until it became a proverb for it and a metonymy for it.
We add to the foregoing what Imam al-Zamakhsharī set forth in his enchanting style, and this is its text:
«If you say: He made the wing, which is the hand, drawn in in one of the two places and drawn to in the other, namely His saying: «وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ», and in Ṭā Hā «وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلى جَناحِكَ»; so how are the two reconciled? I say: what is meant by the wing that is drawn in is the right hand, and what it is drawn to is the left hand, and each one of the right and left hands is a wing».

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(قال ربّ): its i'rab has been given [Note: in āya (16) of this sūra.]; (منهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (نفسا); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle, and (النون) in (يقتلون) is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), which came before the yāʾ of the speaker that was deleted to suit the verse-endings (fawāṣil), and it [Translator's note: i.e. the deleted yāʾ] is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, for seeking mercy.
The clause «إنّي قتلت ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «قتلت» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أخاف» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause قتلت [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, conjoined to the vocative clause.].
The clause «يقتلون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يقتلون ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb of fearing.
(34) (الواو) is a conjunction; (هارون) is a nominative ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of أخي; (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being أفصح; (منّي) is attached to أفصح; (لسانا) is an accusative tamyīz (specification); (الفاء) is a conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (معي) is an accusative adverb attached to the verb أرسله; (ردءا) is an accusative ḥāl of the object of أرسله, and (النون) in (يصدّقني) is for protection; (أن يكذّبون) is like أن يقتلون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكذّبون) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أخاف.

* Morphology:
(أفصح) is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral فصح; its pattern is أفعل.
(ردءا) is the maṣdar of ردأته, meaning "I helped him", and it has the sense of the passive participle; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted, رِدْءاً يُصَدِّقُنِي.
The purpose of his confirming him is not that he should say to him: "You have spoken the truth", or that people should say: "Moses has spoken the truth"; rather it is that he should set out the truth clearly with his tongue, expound the speech about it and dispute with the disbelievers by it. That runs the course of useful confirmation, so confirming was attributed to Aaron, because he is the cause of it, as a figurative attribution. The meaning of figurative attribution is: confirmation is literally in the one who confirms, so attributing it to him is literal; there is no confirmation in the cause, but the attribution was borrowed for it because it is connected with confirmation by causing it, just as the agent is connected with it by doing it directly. The proof of this interpretation is His saying: إِنِّي أَخافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ

* Benefits:
1- أخاف أن يقتلون:
This nūn in «يقتلون» is for protection; as for the nūn of the nominative, it is deleted, and the yāʾ of the speaker was also deleted for the pause at the end of the āya, and for the perfection of the Quranic composition (naẓm) of which we have spoken repeatedly.
2- Philology (fiqh al-lugha):
The scholars of language and its philologists agree that the two letters «ع and ض», when they occur as the fāʾ and ʿayn (first and second radicals) of the verb, indicate strength and hardness, even though they are not many in the world of verbs or nouns.
Among these are «العضل، والعضد، وعضّ، وعضد، وعضب، وعضل». All of this group of verbs contains the sense of strength and hardness. This is another of the secrets of our wondrous language, possessed of special features and secrets.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(بأخيك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نشدّ), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ; (لكما) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is نجعل; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (إليكما) is attached to (يصلون); (بآياتنا) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذهب" [Note: The verb is stated explicitly in another āya ... and it may be attached to (نجعل) or to (يصلون), or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of address ...]; (أنتما) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the detached pronoun by the wāw; (الغالبون) is the khabar (predicate).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سنشدّ..» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «نجعل ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «لا يصلون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause نجعل.
The clause «(اذهب) بآياتنا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «أنتما ... الغالبون ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) - or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) - and the clause «اتّبعكما ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, قالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ.
The state of Moses, peace be upon him, in being strengthened by his brother, is likened to the state of the hand in being strengthened by a strong upper arm. It is also possible that there is a metonymic trope (majāz mursal), of the type of applying the cause to the effect by two degrees, the original being: "We will strengthen you by him", then "We will support you", then "We will strengthen your arm by him".

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (لمّا جاءهم موسى) is like لمّا قضى موسى [Note: in āya (29) of this sūra.]; (بآياتنا) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of موسى; (بيّنات) is an accusative ḥāl of آياتنا; (ما) is negative, inoperative (muhmala); (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (سحر) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هذا; (ما) is like the first; (بهذا) is attached to (سمعنا); (في آبائنا) is attached to a ḥāl of هذا, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: في أيام آبائنا الأولين (in the days of our forefathers).
The clause «جاءهم موسى ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما هذا إلّا سحر..» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما سمعنا..» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
(37) (الواو) is a conjunction; (بمن) is attached to أعلم; (بالهدى) is attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جاء; (من عنده) is attached to (جاء); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من) is a relative in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first relative من; (له) is attached to the khabar of تكون [Note: Or attached to (تكون) if it is complete (tāmma), and (عاقبة) is the agent.]; the hāʾ in (إنّه) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of إنّ; (لا) is negative ...
The clause «قال موسى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قالوا.
The clause «ربّي أعلم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «جاء بالهدى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «تكون له عاقبة ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «إنّه لا يفلح الظالمون» has no grammatical position: a resumption, either within the scope of the speech or from the speech of Allah the Exalted.
The clause «لا يفلح الظالمون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:38-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (أيّها) is an intended indefinite munādā (one addressed), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative; (الملأ) is a badal (substitute) of أيّ, following it in the nominative in form; (ما) is negative; (لكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of إله [Note: This is if the verb علمت is transitive to one object; if it is transitive to two, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).]; (إله) is genitive in form and accusative in position, a mafʿūl bihi whose governor is علمت; (غيري) is a naʿt (adjective) of إله [Note: Or it is a second mafʿūl bihi if the verb علمت is transitive to two, and لكم is a ḥāl.], following it in the genitive in form, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) is resumptive; (لي) is attached to (أوقد); (هامان) is a singular proper-noun munādā, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative; (على الطين) is attached to (أوقد), and على has the meaning of في; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لي) is attached to a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is اجعل; (إلى إله) is attached to (أطّلع); (الواو) is parenthetical - or a conjunction -; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (من الكاذبين) is attached to a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is أظنّه.
The clause «قال فرعون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ما علمت ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «أوقد ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The vocative clause «يا هامان ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «اجعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أوقد ...
The clause «لعلّي أطّلع ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) - or causal (taʿlīliyya) - and the clause «أطّلع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.
The clause «إنّي لأظنّه ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical - or conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «أظنّه ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(39) (الواو) is a conjunction; (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun that is the agent of استكبر; (جنوده) is conjoined to the latent pronoun that is the agent of استكبر; (في الأرض) is attached to (استكبر); (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl of the agent and what is conjoined to it; (إلينا) is attached to the negated (يرجعون), and (الواو) in (يرجعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «استكبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال فرعون.
The clause «ظنّوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استكبر.
The clause «لا يرجعون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّهم إلينا لا يرجعون) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّوا.
(40) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (جنوده) is conjoined to the third-person object pronoun in (أخذناه); (في اليمّ) is attached to (نبذناهم); (الفاء) is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كان ...
The clause «أخذناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ظنّوا ...
The clause «نبذناهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أخذناه.
The clause «انظر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان عاقبة ...» is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi whose governor is the verb of looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative كيف.
(41) (الواو) is a conjunction; (أئمة) is a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, whose governor is جعلناهم; (إلى النار) is attached to (يدعون); (الواو) is a conjunction; (يوم) is an accusative adverb attached to the negated (ينصرون), and (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «جعلناهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نبذناهم.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of أئمة.
The clause «لا ينصرون ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يدعون.
(42) (الواو) is a conjunction; (في هذه) is attached to a ḥāl of لعنة, which is the second object; (الواو) is a conjunction; (يوم) is like the first, attached to المقبوحين [Note: The grammarians do not accept this attachment, claiming that what comes after the relative (ال) does not govern what precedes it, so they attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted verb explained by His saying (من المقبوحين), i.e. they were made vile on the Day of Resurrection ... But the Quranic evidences for the permissibility of the attachment are many ... It may also be conjoined to the position of (في هذه) with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. and the curse of the Day of Resurrection.]; (من المقبوحين) is attached to the omitted khabar of هم.
The clause «أتبعناهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause جعلناهم ...
The clause «هم من المقبوحين ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أتبعناهم ...

* Morphology:
(هامان) is the proper name of Pharaoh's vizier, a foreign word; its pattern is فاعال if it is of Arabic origin.
(المقبوحين) is the plural of المقبوح, a passive participle from the triliteral (قبح), of the class of كرم, the opposite of حسن (to be good), meaning to be driven away and cast off; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Prolixity (al-iṭnāb): in His saying, the Exalted, فَأَوْقِدْ لِي يا هامانُ عَلَى الطِّينِ.
He did not say: "Bake bricks (الآجر) for me and make use of them". That was to avoid mentioning the word الآجر, because its structure - despite the ease of its pronunciation - is not eloquent, and that is a matter which taste alone decides. This expression is more in harmony with the eloquence of the Qur'an and the loftiness of its level, and more like the speech of tyrants.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (الكتاب) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is آتينا; (من بعد) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آتينا); (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (بصائر) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) of الكتاب, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. ذا بصائر (possessing insights) [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما أهلكنا ...) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(للناس) is attached to بصائر [Note: Or to a naʿt (adjective) of بصائر.]; (هدى، رحمة) are two nouns conjoined to بصائر, accusative.
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لعلّهم يتذكّرون.» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتذكّرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ ...

safi-cedvel:44-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (بجانب) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كنت; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative, attached to the khabar of كنت; (إلى موسى) is attached to (قضينا) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the sense of أوحينا (We revealed); (ما) is like the first; (من الشاهدين) is the khabar of كنت.
The clause «ما كنت بجانب..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قضينا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «ما كنت من الشاهدين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(45) (الواو) is a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء); (عليهم) is attached to (تطاول); (ما) is like the first; (في أهل) is attached to (ثاويا); (عليهم) is attached to (تتلو) ...
The clause «لكنّا أنشأنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أنشأنا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّا.
The clause «تطاول ... العمر» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause أنشأنا.
The clause «ما كنت ثاويا» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لكنّا ...
The clause «تتلو ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (ثاويا) [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a second khabar of (كان).].
The clause «لكنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لكنّا أنشأنا.
The clause «كنّا مرسلين» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّا ...
(46) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما كنت ... نادينا) is like ما كنت ... قضينا; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكن) is for rectification (istidrāk); (رحمة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أرسلناك"; (من ربّك) is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة; (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (تنذر) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; (ما) is negative; (نذير) is genitive in form and nominative in position, the agent of أتى; (من قبلك) is attached to (أتاهم).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تنذر ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb أرسلناك.
The clause «ما كنت بجانب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ما كنت ثاويا.
The clause «نادينا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «(أرسلناك) رحمة ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ما كنت ...
The clause «تنذر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ما أتاهم» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (قوما).
The clause «لعلّهم يتذكّرون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتذكّرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لعلّهم.
(47) (الواو) is a conjunction; (لولا) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ - which is causal -, attached to (تصيبهم); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (يقولوا) is accusative, conjoined to (تصيبهم), and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تصيبهم) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar being omitted, its implied form being "موجود" (existing).
(ربّنا) is a muḍāf munādā (one addressed), accusative; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (إلينا) is attached to (أرسلت); (الفاء) is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya); (نتّبع) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and the agent is نحن; (نكون) is a defective verb, accusative, conjoined to (نتّبع) by the wāw; (من المؤمنين) is the khabar of نكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نتّبع) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the preceding urging, i.e.: "Why was there not a sending, and then a following of the signs ..."
The clause «لولا (الإصابة) ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ما كنت ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "We would not have sent messengers to them" [Note: i.e. were it not for their saying, when a calamity strikes them, "Why did You not send a messenger?", We would not have sent a messenger.].
The clause «تصيبهم مصيبة» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قدّمت أيديهم..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the returning pronoun is implied.
The clause «يقولوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تصيبهم مصيبة.
The vocative clause and its response ... is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لولا أرسلت ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «نتّبع ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نكون من المؤمنين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نتّبع.
(48) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لمّا) is an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the apodosis قالوا; (من عندنا) is attached to (جاءهم); (لولا) is like the last one, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (أوتي) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring to Muḥammad ﷺ; (مثل) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) - and it is originally the second object -; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. أوتيه; (موسى) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the second verb (أوتي), and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma; (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يكفروا), and the returning pronoun is omitted; (قبل) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (أوتي); (سحران) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هما [Note: i.e. the Torah and the Qur'an.]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (إنّا) is the particle resembling the verb and its noun; (بكلّ) is attached to the khabar (كافرين) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text reads كافرون].
The clause «جاءهم الحقّ ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are conjoined to the preceding resumption.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لولا أوتي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أوتي موسى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لم يكفروا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Did they believe and not disbelieve ..."
The clause «أوتي موسى ... (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «(هما) سحران» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «تظاهرا ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of (سحران).
The clause «قالوا (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قالوا (the first).
The clause «إنّا بكلّ كافرون» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.

* Morphology:
(45) ثانيا [Translator's note: so in the source, for ثاويا]: an active participle from the triliteral ثوى; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Paronomasia of vowelling (jinās al-taḥrīf): in His saying, the Exalted, وَلكِنَّا كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ.
Jinās al-taḥrīf is that in which the vowelling (ḍabṭ) is what distinguishes between the two words or parts of them.

* Benefits:
- The selection of words.
We saw fit to point briefly to the place of the selection of words in rhetoric and literature. The truth about which there is no dispute is that choosing the word and putting it in its place according to the situation and the requirements of the context is a gift not attained by practice alone, and a faculty given to only a few people - especially since you are before a language whose synonymous vocabulary is abundant, each word having a setting that is determined by taste and a literary faculty that is not subject to rule and is not weighed on a scale. Perhaps wide reading, attending to lofty literary models by reading them, and frequent engagement with them are among what develops and refines this faculty until it is complete or approaches completeness.
In the Noble Qur'an it is at the highest rank of excellence of selection and the faculty of choice.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(عليك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نتلو), and likewise (من نبأ) [Note: من is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); it may be partitive, in which case the prepositional phrase is a naʿt (adjective) of the implied object, i.e. "something of the tidings of Mūsā ..."]; (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of نتلو or of its object; (لقوم) is attached to (نتلو), i.e. "for the sake of ...".
The clause «تلك آيات ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «نتلو ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (تلك), the link being implied, i.e. نتلوها ...; and (آيات) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, or it is a second khabar ... It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of آيات, the governor being the demonstrative.].
The clause «يؤمنون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of قوم.

safi-cedvel:49-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (بكتاب) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ائتوا), and likewise (من عند); (منهما) is attached to أهدى; (أتّبعه) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the command; (كنتم) is a defective past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ائتوا ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If you are truthful in what you say, then bring ..." and the implied conditional clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «هو أهدى ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب.
The clause «أتّبعه ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كنتم صادقين» has no grammatical position: explicative, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
(50) (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the second links to the apodosis; (يستجيبوا) is jussive as the protasis, and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn; (لك) is attached to (يستجيبوا); (أنّما) is the restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); (الواو) is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (أضل); (ممّن) is attached to أضلّ; (بغير) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of اتّبع; (من الله) is attached to a naʿt of هدى; (لا) is negative ...
The clause «لم يستجيبوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «اعلم ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يتّبعون ...» is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the suspended (muʿallaq) verb of knowing [Note: Or we say: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) أَنَّما يَتَّبِعُونَ ... is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of اعلم. The restrictive (ما) is not taken into account, since (أنّ) remains maṣdar-forming ... See āya (52) of Sūrat Ibrāhīm.].
The clause «من أضلّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّبع ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «إنّ الله لا يهدي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا يهدي» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Benefits:
- The elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl):
Although we have dealt with this form before, we prefer to return to it to explain some important features of it:
a- The elative noun has a single pattern, «أفعل», and its feminine is «فعلى», as in أفضل and فضلى [Translator's note: the source prints فضلي]. The hamza of «أفعل» has been deleted in three words, «خير، شر، حبّ», as in the poet's saying:
منعت شيئا فأكثرت الولوع به ... وحبّ شيء إلى الإنسان ما منعا
(You were denied a thing, so you became all the more infatuated with it; the dearest thing to a person is what is withheld.)
The origin of these three is أخير، أشرّ، أحبّ, and their hamza was deleted because of their frequent use.
b- The conditions for forming it:
The elative noun is formed only from a triliteral verb that is affirmative, fully conjugable (mutaṣarrif), active, complete (tāmm) and admitting of degree, provided that it does not indicate a colour, a defect or a physical feature.
c- If we want to form the elative from a verb that does not fulfil the conditions, we bring its maṣdar in the accusative after «أشدّ» or «أكثر» or the like, as in: "So-and-so is more black (أكثر سوادا) than so-and-so."
d- The cases in which it occurs:
The elative noun occurs in four cases:
1- Free of «أل» and of annexation (iḍāfa).
2- Made definite by «ال».
3- Annexed to a definite noun.
4- Annexed to an indefinite noun.
A remark: the elative noun may occur stripped of the sense of comparison, as in:
إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا ... بيتا دعائمه أعزّ وأفضل
(He who raised the heaven built for us a house whose pillars are mightiest and most excellent.)
i.e. mighty and tall. Concerning the elative noun there are exceptions, remarks and details which we have passed over, so that you may return to them in the longer works.

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (لهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وصّلنا) ...
The clause «قد وجملة القسم وصّلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath; the implied [one] has no grammatical position: resumptive. [Translator's note: the source text is garbled here; the intended sense is evidently: the clause «قد وصّلنا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being resumptive.]
The clause «لعلّهم يتذكّرون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يتذكّرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:52-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين) is a relative, mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of the nominative; (من قبله) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آتيناهم); (هم) is a detached pronoun, a second mubtadaʾ, in the position of the nominative; (به) is attached to (يؤمنون), and it [Translator's note: i.e. the clause يؤمنون] is their khabar (predicate).
The clause «الذين آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «هم به يؤمنون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يؤمنون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(53) (الواو) is a conjunction, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (يتلى) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. the Qur'an; (عليهم) is attached to (يتلى); (به) is attached to (آمنّا); (من ربنّا) is attached to an omitted second khabar of (إنّ) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحقّ, the governor of which is the sense of emphasis in the particle resembling the verb.]; (إنّا) is the particle resembling the verb and its noun; (من قبله) is attached to the khabar مسلمين.
The clause «يتلى ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنّا به ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّه الحقّ من ربّنا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) - or causal (taʿlīliyya) -.
The clause «إنّا كنّا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech - or causal -.
The clause «كنّا من قبله مسلمين» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
(54) The wāw in (يؤتون) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (مرّتين) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the bāʾ is causal ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما صبروا) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يؤتون).
(بالحسنة) is attached to (يدرءون); (ممّا) is attached to (ينفقون) - (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle, or a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted -.
The clause «أولئك يؤتون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يؤتون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «صبروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «يدرءون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يؤتون.
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «ينفقون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يؤتون.
(55) (الواو) is a conjunction; (عنه) is attached to (أعرضوا); (لنا) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أعمالنا), and like it (لكم) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أعمالكم; (سلام) is a nominative mubtadaʾ [Note: The mubtadaʾ came indefinite because it indicates generality in praise.], its khabar being the preposition and its genitive noun (عليكم); (لا) is negative ...
The clause «سمعوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أعرضوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «لنا أعمالنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «لكم أعمالكم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «سلام عليكم ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «لا نبتغي ...» has no grammatical position: causal.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) is negative; (الواو) is a conjunction in both places; (بالمهتدين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم in the sense of عالم (knowing).
The clause «إنّك لا تهدي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تهدي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أحببت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «لكنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يهدي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «هو أعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يهدي [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of يهدي, after the wāw of the ḥāl.].

* Benefits:
- إنك لا تهدي من أحببت.
It appears that there is a consensus among the Muslims that this āya was revealed concerning «Abū Ṭālib ...»
when death came to him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "O uncle, say lā ilāha illā Allāh, a word by which I may plead for you before Allah." He said: "O son of my brother, I know that you are truthful, but I dislike that it be said: he lost his nerve at death. Were it not that it would bring disgrace on you and on the sons of your father, I would have said it and gladdened your eye with it at parting, because of what I see of the intensity of your feeling and your sincere counsel." And he recited:
لولا الملامة أو حذار مسبة ... لو جدتني سمحا بذاك مبينا
(Were it not for blame or fear of reproach, you would have found me openly generous in that.)

ولقد علمت بأن دين محمد ... من خير أديان البرية دينا
(I have known that the religion of Muḥammad is among the best of the religions of mankind.)

"But I shall die upon the creed of the elders, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Hāshim and ʿAbd Manāf."
This āya has come to run the course of a proverb, which people circulate in every similar situation, just as many āyas have run the course of proverbs. So reflect ...

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (نتّبع) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; (معك) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نتبع); (من أرضنا) is attached to the passive (نتخطّف); (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لهم) is attached to (نمكّن); (إليه) is attached to (يجبى); (ثمرات) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يجبى; (رزقا) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) - and it is a maṣdar - since it coincides with its verb in meaning, (يجبى) meaning "they are provided in it with provision"; or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. يرزقون رزقا ...; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of an implied verb, i.e. نسوقه رزقا, and in this there is weakness.] of ثمرات, and it is in the sense of "that with which one is provided"; (من لدنّا) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (رزقا); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative ...
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن نتّبع ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «نتخطّف ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لم نمكّن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: "Did We leave them and not establish for them ..."
The clause «يجبى إليه ثمرات ...» is in the position of the accusative as a second naʿt of (حرما) [Note: Or a ḥāl of (حرما), because it is described.].
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the implied resumption.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لكنّ.

* Morphology:
(حرما) is either an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حرم يحرم, of the class of فرح, meaning "it was forbidden to them", or a noun for what is defended and what may not be violated ...; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas, and by it is meant Mecca and its sanctuary.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted, أَوَلَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَهُمْ حَرَماً آمِناً.
Because those who are literally safe are its inhabitants. Like it is «وكم أهلكنا من قرية ...», where what is meant is its people.

safi-cedvel:58-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (كم) is declarative (khabariyya), an allusive term for number, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من قرية) is the tamyīz (specification) of كم; (معيشتها) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi whose governor is بطرت, by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the sense of خسرت (it lost) [Note: It may be accusative as an adverb with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "it exulted during the days of its livelihood", or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "it exulted in its livelihood".]; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (مساكنهم) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) تلك, nominative (marfūʿ); (من بعدهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated (تسكن); (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (قليلا) is accusative as the excepted [Note: That from which the exception is made is implied: it may be a time, a place or a maṣdar (verbal noun), and (قليلا) stands in for the excepted time, place or maṣdar, i.e. "they were not inhabited for any period, or in any place, or by any inhabiting, except for a little time, a little place or a little inhabiting".]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (نحن) is a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun نا ...
The clause «أهلكنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «بطرت ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of قرية.
The clause «تلك مساكنهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أهلكنا.
The clause «لم تسكن من بعدهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of مساكنهم, its governor being the demonstrative [Note: Or it is a second khabar of the demonstrative تلك ... or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), and so has no grammatical position.].
The clause «كنّا ... الوارثين ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause لم تسكن, with an implied linking pronoun, i.e. الوارثين لها منهم (the inheritors of them from them) - or in the position of the nominative, or with no grammatical position -.
(59) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (يبعث) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتّى; (في أمّها) is attached to (يبعث); (عليهم) is attached to (يتلو) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبعث ...) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to the active participle مهلك.
