(الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is like the first; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (الواو) is the wāw of the ḥāl.
The clause «ما كان ربّك مهلك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يبعث ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يتلو ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (رسولا).
The clause «ما كنّا مهلكي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ما كان ربّك..
The clause «أهلها ظالمون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and it is excepted from the most general of states,
i.e. We were not destroyers of the towns in any state of all states except in the state of their being wrongdoers.

* Benefits:
- The shortened noun (al-ism al-maqṣūr) and the curtailed noun (al-ism al-manqūṣ):
a- Their i'rab:
All three vowels are implied on the alif in the maqṣūr noun, and it is said: "because of impossibility (lil-taʿadhdhur)", i.e. it is impossible to show them. The ḍamma and the kasra are implied on the yāʾ of the manqūṣ, and the fatḥa is shown.
b- If the maqṣūr takes tanwīn, the tanwīn is pronounced at its end, and the shortened alif is dropped in pronunciation and remains in writing. If the manqūṣ takes tanwīn, its yāʾ is dropped in pronunciation and writing in the nominative and genitive, while in the accusative the vowel and the tanwīn both appear on it, and an alif is added at its end as a seat for the tanwīn.
c- The manqūṣ regularly ends in a vowelless yāʾ. The maqṣūr ends in a vowelless alif, written as an alif if its origin is a wāw, or drawn as a vowelless yāʾ if it is converted from a yāʾ, i.e. if the origin of its verb is yāʾ-final.
d- To know the origin of the verb from which the maqṣūr or manqūṣ noun is taken, whether it is wāw-based or yāʾ-based, we resort to the following procedures:
First: we join the past verb to the vowelled tāʾ of the agent, as in: غزا، غزوت.
Second: we take its imperfect, as in رمى يرمي.
Third: we derive the maṣdar from it, as in سعى سعيا.
Fourth: we make it dual or plural, as in: عصا عصوان, etc.

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (التاء) in (أوتيتم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the verb is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من شيء) is the tamyīz (specification) of ما; (الفاء) links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (متاع) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو; (زينتها) is conjoined to متاع by the wāw, nominative like it; (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being خير; (عند) is an accusative adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative.
The clause «أوتيتم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «متاع الحياة ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما عند الله خير ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا تعقلون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Have you been heedless, so that you do not reason?"

* Benefits:
عند:
An adverb of place and an adverb of time. You say: عند الحائط (by the wall) and عند الصباح (at morning). It is always accusative as an adverb. It is made genitive by من, so one says: من عنده. The common people's saying ذهبت إلى عنده is a solecism. And «عند ...» is always annexed, so it is not used alone, i.e. without annexation (iḍāfa).

safi-cedvel:61-62.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) is resumptive; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (وعدا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (كمن) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ من; (متاع) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq; (ثمّ) is a conjunction; (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to المحضرين; (من المحضرين) is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هو.
The clause «من وعدناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «وعدناه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (من).
The clause «هو لاقيه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «متّعناه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «هو ... من المحضرين.» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause متّعناه.
(62) (الواو) is a conjunction; (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر", and the agent of (يناديهم) is a pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. Allah; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (أين) is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (شركائي); (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of شركائي, and the two objects of (تزعمون) are omitted, indicated by the preceding speech, i.e. تزعمونهم شركاء (you claim them to be partners).
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يناديهم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يناديهم.
The clause «أين شركائي ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «كنتم تزعمون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تزعمون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كنتم.

* Morphology:
(61) لاقيه: an active participle from the triliteral (لقي); its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
- أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ.
تزعمون: the verb (زعم) takes two objects in the accusative, but they have been omitted because they are known from the context of the speech, i.e. تزعمونهم أربابا (you claim them to be lords). The permissibility of omitting the two objects applies regularly to all the verbs that take two objects, when this condition is fulfilled, namely that they are known from the context of the speech.
Al-Kumayt said, praising the Family of the House:
بأي كتاب أم بأية سنة ... ترى حبهم عارا عليّ وتحسب
(By what Book, or by what Sunna, do you consider love of them a disgrace upon me, and reckon [it so]?)
i.e. تحسب حبهم عارا عليّ ... and what preceded them of the speech indicated them.

* Rhetoric:
The explicit, dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَنْباءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ.
Its origin is "they became blind to the tidings", i.e. they were not guided to them, blindness having been borrowed for lack of guidance; then it was inverted for intensification, so the tidings were made not to find their way to them, and blindness was made to contain the sense of being hidden, so it was made transitive with على; were it not for that, it would have been made transitive with عن. It was not connected with the tidings [Translator's note: i.e. blindness was not literally attributed to the tidings as something seen], because they are heard, not seen. In this inversion there is an indication that what comes to the mind flows onto it and reaches it from outside. It is also possible that there is in the speech an implicit, imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya), i.e. the tidings became as if blind to them, not finding their way to them.

* Morphology:
(7) خفت: it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion, in keeping with the verb being indeclinable on the sukūn. Its origin is خافت with sukūn on the fāʾ; when two quiescent letters met, the weak letter was dropped, and the khāʾ was given kasra to match the vowel of the verb's ʿayn, since it belongs to the fourth class; its pattern is فلت with kasra on the fāʾ.
(8) حزنا: maṣdar of the triliteral حزن in the sense of أحزن — أحزن, of the نصر class; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and the maṣdar is used in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "a cause of grief to them".
(7) ألقيه: it contains a weak-letter change by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, starting from the imperfect تلقين ...: the yāʾ of the verb met the yāʾ of the addressed feminine — both quiescent — so the lām of the word was dropped; its pattern is أفعيه.
(10) فارغا: active participle of the triliteral فرغ; its pattern is فاعل.
(12) المراضع: plural of مرضع — or مرضعة —, the active participle of the quadriliteral أرضع; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in the words of Allah the Exalted إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَها شِيَعاً يَسْتَضْعِفُ طائِفَةً مِنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْناءَهُمْ.
Here the slaughtering is attributed to Pharaoh, though he is not the real agent; he only ordered the slaughter, and Pharaoh's soldiers are the real agents. So the attribution of the word "slaughter" to Pharaoh is figurative.
Amplification (al-iṭnāb): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَلا تَخافِي وَلا تَحْزَنِي.
This is a rare kind, among the most beautiful kinds of amplification: a thing is mentioned and expressed with overlapping meanings, except that each meaning has a particular feature that the other does not have. Fear is a distress that befalls a person on account of something expected, and grief is a distress that befalls him on account of something that has happened — namely his separation [from her] and the dangers surrounding him. So she was forbidden them all, was made secure by the revelation to her, and was promised what would console her, set her heart at rest and fill it with happiness and joy.
Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَحَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِ الْمَراضِعَ.
التحريم ("forbidding") is a metaphor for prevention, because whoever has a thing forbidden to him has been prevented from it; do you not see their saying محظور and حجر? That is because Allah prevented him from sucking any breast, so he would never accept the breast of a wet-nurse, until that worried them.

* Benefits:
1- The script of the Qur'an:
We have said before that the script of the Noble Qur'an differs in many of its words from the agreed-upon spelling in writing the Arabic language, and we give as examples of this these from this āya:
«ايت، نتلوا، همن».
In the first the alif is omitted; in the second the alif is placed after the wāw, whereas it should not be placed, because the wāw is part of the root of the word; in the third the quiescent alif is omitted. This is frequent in the Noble Qur'an, and it needs someone to survey it inductively and produce it in a treatise.
2- Novelty of expression: a- أَصْبَحَ فُؤادُ أُمِّ مُوسى فارِغاً.
b- لَوْلا أَنْ رَبَطْنا عَلى قَلْبِها.
c- فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِ عَنْ جُنُبٍ.
These three examples of Quranic expression, and many others like them in the Noble Qur'an, present us with a clear picture of creativity and innovation in Arabic style, which no writer or poet has reached or come near to, closely or remotely. It is revelation, sent down from the Lord of the Worlds, to present to people a picture of inimitability, that perhaps they may believe in it; yet most people were not believers.
3- فرعون and هامان:
Two foreign nouns, diptotes (barred from full declension); what bars them is their being proper names and foreign. For this reason they take fatḥa in the genitive. We have pointed out before that a noun is not barred from full declension unless it contains two of the causes that bar it, except in two cases, where one cause suffices. The two cases are:
the two forms of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ), مفاعل and مفاعيل; and the alif of the feminine, whether extended or shortened, e.g. حمراء, سلوى and ليلى.
a- An important observation: the form of the ultimate plural bars from full declension whether it is a real plural or the name of a singular that comes on the form of the ultimate plural, e.g. «شراحيل وسراويل».
b- The causes that bar from full declension:
a- The form of the ultimate plural.
b- The extended and shortened alif of the feminine.
c- Being a proper name (ʿalamiyya), which has seven cases:
1- The feminine with tāʾ marbūṭa, or the feminine in meaning; the first like فاطمة, the second like سعاد.
2- The foreign proper name, like إبراهيم and انطون.
3- The proper name on the pattern of a verb, like يشكر and يزيد.
4- The proper name compounded by blending (tarkīb mazjī), e.g. بعلبك.
5- The proper name with an added alif and nūn, e.g. عثمان.
6- The proper name diverted (maʿdūl) onto the pattern (فعل), e.g. عمر.
7- The proper name with an alif of assimilation (ilḥāq) added at its end, like أرطى and ذفرى.
d- The adjective, which has three cases:
1- That the adjective be on the pattern «أفعل», like «أحمر وأفضل».
2- That the adjective be on the pattern «فعلان», like «عطشان وسكران».
3- That the adjective be «diverted» (maʿdūla), which is in two places:
a- In numbers, like «أحاد وموحد», ثناء and مثنى, ثلاث and مثلث, etc.
b- The second is «أخر», e.g. مررت بنساء أخر ("I passed by other women").
4- The lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba):
The Basrans rejected calling it the lām of consequence, and al-Zamakhsharī called it "the lām of cause" (lām al-ʿilla), the cause in it being figurative, not real. That is because the motive for picking him up was not that he should be an enemy and a grief to them, but their love for him and the desire to adopt him [Translator's note: the source reads «وبغية تنبيه», most likely a misprint for «تبنّيه» ("adopting him"), which is the sense translated.] — like someone saying «ضربته ليتأدب» ("I struck him so that he would learn manners"). In reality they picked him up out of love, but its consequence was enmity. For this reason the lām is called «the lām of consequence».
5- Mūsā and Pharaoh:
It is related, concerning the Arabicisation of the word «موسى», that «مو» is water and «سا» is trees; perhaps they likened «موسى» to water and trees, which spring from the earth, because they picked him up from the river and knew of no father or mother for him, but found him among them. He is Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, and his lineage goes back to «Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm».
Israel remained in Egypt from the time of Yūsuf to the time of Mūsā, i.e. the time of the Pharaoh to whom Mūsā was sent. This Pharaoh was exceedingly insolent and harsh and long-lived; his name was «al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab». He took the Children of Israel as virtual slaves, building and ploughing for him, and he levied the jizya from the rest of them. He saw in a dream a fire that came from the direction of Jerusalem and burned the Copts. He asked for the interpretation of his dream and was told: a man will come forth from the Children of Israel at whose hand Egypt will perish. So he ordered every child born to the Children of Israel to be killed, until he almost annihilated them; then he changed his mind and began killing their sons one year and sparing them the next. Hārūn was born in the year in which the sons were not killed, and Mūsā was born in the year in which they were killed. When his mother gave birth to him she grieved, and Allah revealed to her: put him in a chest, then cast it into the river. So she made a chest, put him in it, cast it into the Nile, and said to his sister: follow him. The water carried him until it brought him in among dense trees beneath Pharaoh's palace. Pharaoh's slave-girls came out to bathe and found the chest, and we brought it in to Āsiya, Pharaoh's wife [Translator's note: the source has «فأدخلناه» ("we brought it in"), probably for «فأدخلنه» ("they brought it in").]. When she saw him she loved him, and she told Pharaoh about him. He wanted to slaughter him, fearing that he might be the child he had been warned of, but Āsiya kept at him until he left him to her. That is the word of Allah the Exalted فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً. We shall continue the narration of the story in the light of the following āyas, if Allah wills.

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive; (أمّا) is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl); (من) is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: (من) has been parsed as a relative noun so that two conditional particles do not occur together.]; (صالحا) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الفاء) links to the response of أمّا; (عسى) is a complete (tāmm) past verb, for expectation or for realization; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يكون) is in the position of the nominative as the agent of عسى.
(من المفلحين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكون.
The clause «من تاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تاب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «آمن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «عمل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «عسى أن يكون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:68-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second (ما) is negative; (لهم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (سبحان) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; the third (ما) is maṣdar-forming [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما يشركون) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (تعالى).
The clause «ربّك يخلق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يخلق ما يشاء ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ربّك).
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يختار ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يخلق.
The clause «ما كان لهم الخيرة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعالى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause (نسبّح).
The clause «يشركون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما) ...
(69) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ربّك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم) is like ربّك يخلق ما يشاء; (ما يعلنون) is conjoined to (ما تكنّ ...)
The clause «ربّك يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ربّك يخلق.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ربّك).
The clause «تكنّ صدورهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «يعلنون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
(70) (الواو) is a conjunction; (إلّا) is a particle of exception; (هو) is a detached pronoun, a badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar of لا; (له) is attached to the khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ الحمد; (في الأولى) is attached to الحمد; (الواو) is a conjunction; (له الحكم) is like له الحمد; (إليه) is attached to (ترجعون), and (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «هو الله ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ربّك يعلم.
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو ...» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), and likewise له الحمد.].
The clause «له الحمد ...» is in the position of the nominative as a third khabar.
The clause «له الحكم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause له الحمد.
The clause «ترجعون ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause له الحمد.

* Morphology:
(68) الخيرة: a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the verb تخيّر, so it has the meaning of التخيّر, or of the verb اختار, in the sense of الاختيار (choosing) ... In al-Miṣbāḥ: الخيرة with fatḥa on the yāʾ means الخيار, and الخيار is choosing; and it is said to be a noun from تخيّرت, like الطيرة from تطيّرت. Its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
Embedding (al-idmāj): in His saying, the Exalted, لَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْأُولى وَالْآخِرَةِ.
This device is that the speaker embeds either one purpose in another purpose, or one rhetorical figure in another, in such a way that only one of the two purposes, or one of the two figures, appears in the speech, while the other is embedded in the purpose that is present in the speech. In this āya hyperbole has been embedded in antithesis (al-muṭābaqa), because His being alone, Glorified is He, in receiving praise in the Hereafter - the time when none but He is praised - is hyperbole in describing His Essence with singularity and praise. And even though the speech in these two [Translator's note: so in the source] takes outwardly the form of hyperbole, the matter in it is inwardly literal truth, because He is the most deserving of praise in the two abodes, and is in truth the Lord of praise, thanks and fair commendation in both places; anyone else among all His creation is praised in this world only figuratively, and the reality of his praise returns to the Master of praise, Glorified is He.

safi-cedvel:71-72.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative, and the first object of (رأيتم) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, referring to الليل (the night) [Note: In the speech there is a contention (tanāzuʿ) between the two verbs رأيتم and جعل.]; (جعل) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (عليكم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جعل); (سرمدا) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is جعل [Note: in the sense of صيّر (to make into); if it is in the sense of "created" and "brought into being", it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الليل.]; (إلى يوم) is attached to (سرمدا) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (سرمدا).]; (من) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being إله; (غير) is a naʿt of إله; (بضياء) is attached to (يأتيكم); the second (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرأيتم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إن جعل ...» has no grammatical position, or [Translator's note: the source text is garbled here, repeating: «لا محلّ لها أوجملة: «إن جعل ... » لا محلّ لها»; the intended sense is evidently the following] the clause «إن جعل ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, explained by the interrogative clause mentioned.
The clause «من إله ...» is in the position of the accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi whose governor is رأيتم.
The clause «يأتيكم ...» is in the position of the nominative as a second naʿt of إله [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of إله, because it is described.].
The clause «لا تسمعون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Have you deafened your ears, so that you do not hear?"
(72) (قل أرأيتم ... أفلا تبصرون) is like the previous āya, in its words and clauses ...
The clause «تسكنون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of ليل..

* Morphology:
(سرمدا): a noun meaning "perpetual"; its pattern is فعلل - and not فعمل with the mīm being augmentative, as some have stated -.

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (من رحمته) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جعل), and من is causal; (لكم) is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is جعل; (اللام) is for causation (taʿlīl); (تسكنوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and like it (لتبتغوا); (فيه) is attached to (تسكنوا); (من فضله) is attached to (تبتغوا ...).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تسكنوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (جعل).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبتغوا) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (جعل), so it is conjoined to the first.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تسكنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تبتغوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «لعلّكم تشكرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "that you may be provided for, and that you may give thanks".
The clause «تشكرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:74-75.t:
* I'rab:
(ويوم يناديهم ... تزعمون): its i'rab has been given [Note: in āya (62) of this sūra.], in its words and clauses.
(75) (الواو) is a conjunction; (من كلّ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزعنا) in the sense of أخرجنا (We brought out); (الفاء) is a conjunction in both places; (هاتوا) is an inflexible (jāmid) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, by analogy with its counterparts ...; (لله) is attached to the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الحقّ لله) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of علموا.
(عنهم) is attached to (ضلّ) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the sense of غاب (was absent); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the agent of ضلّ, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. يفترونه.
The clause «نزعنا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يناديهم.
The clause «قلنا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نزعنا.
The clause «هاتوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «علموا ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause قلنا ...
The clause «ضلّ عنهم ما ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause علموا.
The clause «كانوا يفترون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يفترون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(شهيدا), in the sense of الشاهد (the witness), is an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral شهد; its pattern is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Involution and evolution (al-laff wa-l-nashr): in His saying, the Exalted, وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ فَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ.
In this āya there is the method of laff in repeating the rebuke for taking partners: an announcement that nothing brings on the wrath of Allah more than associating partners with Him, just as nothing enters more into His good pleasure than affirming His Oneness.
O Allah, just as You have entered us among the people of Your Oneness, enter us among those saved from Your threat.

* Benefits:
- The inflexible verb (al-fiʿl al-jāmid): We said previously: if the verb is connected with time, that calls for the variation of its forms, and this is the fully conjugable (mutaṣarrif) verb; if it is not connected with time, that necessitates its inflexibility and its keeping to a single form.
What concerns us in this āya is to become acquainted with the inflexible verb «هات ...», for it is one of the inflexible verbs restricted to the imperative, so neither a past nor an imperfect comes from it. There is disagreement whether it is indeclinable on the kasra and fixed in a single state, or whether its indeclinable ending varies with the variation of the pronouns attached to it. Here is an example of that: «قُلْ هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ ...».

safi-cedvel:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(من قوم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (الفاء) is a conjunction; (عليهم) is attached to (بغى); (من الكنوز) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is آتيناه; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (بالعصبة) is attached to (تنوء), and (الباء) is for transitivity (taʿdiya) [Note: Or according to the rule of inversion (qalb), i.e. لتنوء بها العصبة أولو القوّة (a band of strong men would be weighed down by them).]; (أولي) is a naʿt (adjective) of العصبة, genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; (إذ) is an adverbial noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; (له) is attached to (قال); (لا) is the jussive-governing particle of prohibition, and the second is negative.
The clause «إنّ قارون كان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان من قوم موسى ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «بغى عليهم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «آتيناه ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «إنّ مفاتحه لتنوء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «تنوء بالعصبة ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (the second) إنّ.
The clause «(اذكر) إذ قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قال له قومه ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا تفرح ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) - or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) - and the clause «لا يحبّ الفرحين ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (the third) إنّ.
(77) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle - or a relative with the returning pronoun omitted - and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما آتاك ...) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (ابتغ), and (في) is causal.
(الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is the jussive-governing particle of prohibition; (من الدنيا) is attached to نصيب; (ما) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (إليك) is attached to (أحسن).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أحسن ...) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is أحسن; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لا) is like the first; (في الأرض) is attached to الفساد; (لا) is negative.
The clause «ابتغ ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «أتاك الله ...» [Translator's note: so in the source, for آتاك] has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative or nominal relative (ما).
The clause «لا تنس ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «أحسن ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «أحسن الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لا تبغ ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «إنّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: causal - or an explanatory resumption - and the clause «لا يحبّ المفسدين ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(قارون) is the proper name of the paternal uncle of Moses, peace be upon him, or of his paternal cousin..
It is a foreign proper name, a diptote, and its pattern according to the Arabic form is فاعول.

* Rhetoric:
Hyperbole (al-mubālagha): in His saying, the Exalted, ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ أُولِي الْقُوَّةِ.
Hyperbole was used in describing the treasures of Qārūn, in that He mentioned them in the plural, put the keys in the plural too, and mentioned being weighed down, the band and "possessed of strength". It is said that sixty mules used to carry the keys of his storehouses, a key for each storehouse. This hyperbole in the Qur'an is among the finest and most remarkable of hyperboles in the view of the skilled, and it consists in exhaustively covering everything that indicates abundance and the multitude of what relates to what he owns.
Completion (al-tatmīm): in His saying, the Exalted, وَلا تَنْسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيا.
A necessary completion, because if he did not seize the opportunity of it [Translator's note: i.e. of this world] to work for the Hereafter, he would have no share in the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:78-82.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) is the restrictive (kāffa) and restricted (makfūfa); the nominative pronoun in (أوتيته) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (على علم) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil; (عندي) is an accusative adverb attached to a naʿt (adjective) of علم; (الهمزة) is for the disapproving interrogative (istifhām inkārī); (الواو) is a conjunction; (من قبله) is attached to (أهلك); (من القرون) is attached to a ḥāl of the relative من [Note: and (من) is explicative (bayāniyya) ... or it is attached to the verb أهلك, and (من) is partitive.].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ الله قد أهلك..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
(من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being أهلك; (منه) is attached to أشدّ; (قوة) is an accusative tamyīz (specification), and likewise (جمعا); (الواو) is parenthetical; (عن ذنوبهم) is attached to (يسأل); (المجرمون) is the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أوتيته ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لم يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.:
"Was he ignorant and did not know.." or: "Did he know what he claimed and not know ..."
The clause «قد أهلك ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The clause «هو أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «لا يسأل ... المجرمون ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.
(79) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (على قومه) is attached to (خرج); (في زينته) is a ḥāl of the agent of خرج, i.e. adorned; (يا) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (لنا) is attached to the omitted khabar of ليت, and (مثل) is the noun of ليت, accusative; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. أوتيه; (قارون) is the nāʾib fāʿil of the passive أوتي; (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (ذو) is the khabar of إنّ, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «خرج ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال ...
The clause «قال الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يريدون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ليت لنا مثل ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أوتي قارون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّه لذو ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
(80) (الواو) is a conjunction; (ويلكم) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb that is not in use; (لمن) is attached to the khabar خير; (الواو) is parenthetical; (لا) is negative; (إلّا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الصابرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «قال الذين أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال الذين يريدون.
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «ويلكم ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of imprecation.
The clause «ثواب الله خير ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «آمن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «عمل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause آمن.
The clause «لا يلقّاها إلّا الصابرون..» has no grammatical position: parenthetical between the two conjoined elements [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.].
(81) (الفاء) is a conjunction; (به) is attached to (خسفنا), and likewise (بداره), so it is conjoined to the first; (الفاء) is causal; (ما) is negative; (له) is attached to the khabar of كان; (فئة) is genitive in form and nominative in position, the noun of كان; (من دون) is attached to a ḥāl of the agent of ينصرونه; (ما كان) is like the first; (من المنتصرين) is attached to the khabar of كان.
The clause «خسفنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption required by the course of the story.
The clause «ما كان له من فئة..» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «ينصرونه ...» is in the position of the genitive (or the nominative) as a naʿt of فئة [Note: The clause may be the khabar of (كان), in the position of the accusative, and (وله) [Translator's note: so in the source, for له] a ḥāl of فئة.].
The clause «ما كان من المنتصرين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the causal clause.
(82) (الواو) is a conjunction; (مكانه) is an accusative mafʿūl bihi with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. مثل مكانه (the like of his position); (بالأمس) is attached to (تمنّوا); (وي) is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning أعجب (I marvel); (كأنّ) is a particle resembling the verb [Note: For the word (ويكأنه) there are many explanations, of which we have preferred the easiest, simplest and most in accord with the meaning.]; (لمن) is attached to (يبسط); (من عباده) is attached to a ḥāl of the implied returning pronoun [Note: Or a tamyīz of the relative (من).], i.e. يشاء رزقه (He wills to provide for him); (لولا) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (علينا) is attached to (منّ); (اللام) occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of لو [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the āya is لولا]; (بنا) is attached to (خسف).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن منّ الله ...) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar is omitted, i.e. موجود (existing).
(ويكأنّه) is like the first; (لا) is negative ... and (الهاء) in (ويكأنه) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of كأنّ.
The clause «أصبح الذين ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خسفنا ...
The clause «تمنّوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (الذين).
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of أصبح.
The clause «ويكأنّ الله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يبسط الرزق ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of كأنّ.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «يقدر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لولا أن منّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, within the scope of the speech.
The clause «منّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «خسف بنا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ويكأنّه لا يفلح ...» has no grammatical position: another resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «لا يفلح الكافرون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of كأنّ.

* Morphology:
(ويكأنّ): The following appears in the Ḥāshiya of al-Jamal: «On ويكأنّ there are several views. The first: that وي is a word by itself, a verbal noun meaning "I marvel", i.e. I [marvel], and (الكاف) is for causation, and أنّ with what is in its scope is made genitive by it, i.e.: "I marvel because Allah extends provision ..." etc. The second: some said that كأنّ here is for comparison, except that its meaning [of comparison] has gone from it and it has come to express statement and certainty [Note: This is the view we have preferred in the i'rab above.]. The third: that ويك is a word by itself, (الكاف) in it is a particle of address, and (أن) is governed by an omitted [verb], i.e.: "Know that Allah extends ..." etc.; al-Akhfash said this. The fourth: that its origin is ويلك, and the lām was deleted ...
The fifth: that (ويكأنّ) as a whole is independent and simple, and its meaning is "Have you not seen"; this may have been transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās. It is transmitted from al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī - of the Kufans - that it means "Do you not see the work of Allah", and Ibn Qutayba related that it means "mercy upon you" in the dialect of Ḥimyar.. In the Qur'an only ويكأنّ and ويكأنّه are written, joined, in both places..» End of quotation.

* Benefits:
1- The story of Qārūn:
It is a story that stirs souls and feeds pens, and it revolves around a type of person from whom no age or land is free. Therefore it carries a lesson worthy of being a lesson for the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor alike.
It is said: he was the paternal cousin of Moses son of ʿImrān, and it is said: he was his maternal cousin. He is one of those proverbial for abundance of wealth, and he was among the most handsome of people in face and in reciting the Torah; and it is said that he was among the seventy whom Moses chose from his people.
It has been said that he went out riding a grey mule, with seven hundred maidservants on grey mules, wearing jewellery and fine garments, in full adornment, and he almost seduced the Children of Israel. Then he transgressed and exceeded bounds, grew arrogant and tyrannical, until Allah destroyed him. The cause of his destruction was that Moses gave the ḥubūra, which is the imamate [Translator's note: i.e. the priestly leadership], to Aaron, and Qārūn envied him and said to Moses: "You have the messengership and Aaron has the ḥubūra, and I have nothing; I cannot bear this." Moses told him that this was by the command of Allah. Qārūn said: "By Allah, I will never believe you until you bring me a sign." So Moses ordered the chiefs of the Children of Israel each to bring his staff, and they brought them. Moses cast them into a dome [Translator's note: i.e. a tent] of his by the command of Allah, and Moses prayed to Allah to show them the proof of that, and the staff of Aaron stirred, turned green and put forth leaves. Moses said to Qārūn: "Do you not see what Allah the Exalted has done for Aaron?" Qārūn said: "By Allah, this is no more wondrous than the sorcery you perform." Then he withdrew with those of the Children of Israel who were with him - he had much wealth and many followers - and Moses prayed against him, and he perished.
It is also said that when the āya of zakāt was revealed to Moses and Qārūn found what was due from him of wealth to be enormous, he gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and told them that Moses would afflict them in their wealth. They said to him: "You are our elder; command us and we will obey your command."
So Qārūn called a prostitute who was among the people and set her a fee to accuse Moses with regard to herself. Then he called the people to assemble and asked Moses to exhort them. Moses began enumerating the prescribed punishments of Allah, until he said: "Whoever commits fornication, we flog him, and if he is married we stone him." Qārūn said to him: "And if it is you? This woman claims that you committed fornication with her." Moses asked her before an assembly of the people, and she confessed that Qārūn had asked her to accuse Moses of fornication. Moses prostrated to Allah and prayed against Qārūn, and Allah made the earth subject to Moses. He said: "O earth, take him", and it began to swallow him while Moses was saying:
"Take him", and Qārūn was crying for help, and Moses was saying: "Take him", until he disappeared into the depths of the earth. The people who had been magnifying him the day before began to despise him and to praise Allah who had saved them from Qārūn, his delusion and his corrupting of people's hearts.
2- وي.
Concerning «وي ...» there are views, of which we present the most important:
a- وي: a verbal noun of the imperfect meaning أعجب or أتعجب (I marvel), and after the marvelling is over comes the comparison «كأنه لا يصلح الظالمون ...» [Translator's note: so in the source; the āya reads وَيْكَأَنَّهُ لا يُفْلِحُ الْكافِرُونَ]. The exegetes and grammarians held that comparison is not what is intended, but rather affirmation.
b- There is another view: the kāf has been attached to «وي ...», so it became «ويك ...»; this is the kāf of address attached to the verbal noun, and then the speech begins with «أنه لا يُفْلِحُ الْكافِرُونَ ...».
This view is strengthened by the saying of ʿAntara:
ولقد شفى نفسي وأبرأ سقمها ... قيل الفوارس: ويك عنتر أقدم
(What healed my soul and cured its sickness was the horsemen's cry: "Woe to you, ʿAntar, charge!")
c- There is a third view, the gist of which is that the origin of the word is «ويلك ...», and the lām was deleted because of frequent use, so it became «ويك». The grammarians and exegetes did not confine themselves to these three views, but expanded in independent reasoning until they set forth weak views which we can do without mentioning.

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الدار) a badal for تلك - or an adjective - (للذين) attached to (نجعلها) «[Note: this is if the verb contains the sense of a verb transitive to one object, that is "We prepare it"; and if it has the sense of "making into", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted second direct object …]», (لا) a negation (في الأرض) attached to (علوا), (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant, to emphasise the negation (فسادا) conjoined to (علوا), accusative like it (للمتّقين) attached to the predicate of the subject العاقبة.
Clause: «تلك الدار ... نجعلها.» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «نجعلها ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the subject (تلك).
Clause: «لا يريدون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «العاقبة للمتّقين ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Benefits:
- تِلْكَ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ:
The general rule states:
Every noun made definite by «ال» after a demonstrative is an ʿaṭf bayān or a badal.
We have already had a complete review of the demonstratives, so we see no need to return to mentioning them.
We say only of «تلك ...» that it resolves into three words: «ت» a demonstrative for the feminine singular, «اللام» which indicates that the thing pointed to is far, and «الكاف» for address. What indicates the kind of person addressed may also be attached to it, whether masculine or feminine, singular, dual or plural, so we say: تلك, تلكما, تلكم, تلكن.

safi-cedvel:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a conditional noun, a subject whose predicate is the clause جاء (بالحسنة) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جاء (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (له) attached to the fronted predicate of the subject خير (منها) attached to خير (من جاء بالسيّئة) like من جاء بالحسنة (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (الذين) a relative in the position of a nominative, deputy agent (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of an accusative, the object of يجزى, with an omitted muḍāf, and the ʿāʾid omitted, that is: "the recompense of what they used to do".]».
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا..) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, its governing word being يجزى, and in it a muḍāf is omitted, that is "the recompense of their deed".
Clause: «من جاء ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «جاء بالحسنة ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the first subject (من).
Clause: «له خير منها ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
Clause: «من جاء (الثانية) ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من جاء (the first).
Clause: «جاء بالسيّئة ...» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of the second subject (من).
Clause: «لا يجزى الذين ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the implied apodosis, that is: "so for him is the like of it, because those who ... are not recompensed ..."
Clause: «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
Clause: «كانوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
Clause: «يعملون ...» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كانوا ...

safi-cedvel:85-85.t:
* I'rab:
(عليك) attached to (فرض), (اللام) the shifted lām, for emphasis (إلى معاد) attached to the predicate رادّك (أعلم) the predicate of the subject ربي, and it has the sense of عالم, and it has put the direct object (من) in the accusative, (بالهدى) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جاء (الواو) a conjunction, and the second (من) is like the first and conjoined to it (في ضلال) attached to the predicate of the subject هو.
Clause: «إنّ الذي ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «فرض ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive - or parenthetical between the two conjoined elements.
Clause: «ربّي أعلم ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «جاء ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative (من).
Clause: «هو في ضلال ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (من).

* Morphology:
(معاد): a noun of place from the triliteral (عاد); its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it has an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin was معود - with sukūn on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the wāw - the vowel on the wāw was found heavy so it was made sākin, then the vowel was moved to the ʿayn, and when what precedes the wāw was vowelled, it was changed to an alif.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of indefiniteness: in the saying of the Exalted إِلى مَعادٍ:
The reason for making معاد indefinite is that on that day it was a place of return of consequence and a destination of weight, because of the victory of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over Mecca and his overpowering its people, and the manifestation of the might of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism and its party.

safi-cedvel:86-88.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive - or a conjunction (ما) a negation (أن) a maṣdar particle, and the sign of the accusative in (يلقى) is the implied fatḥa on the alif (إليك) attached to (يلقى), (الكتاب) deputy agent of the passive يلقى (إلّا) a particle with the sense of لكن, and the exception is detached (munqaṭiʿ), (رحمة) object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) for an implied governing word, accusative (من ربّك) attached to رحمة (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (لا) a prohibitive that jusses (تكونّن) a defective imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, its subject a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (للكافرين) attached to the predicate of تكوننّ (ظهيرا).
Clause: «ما كنت ترجو ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive «[Note: or conjoined to the clause: «إنّ الذي فرض ...» in the preceding verse (85).]».
Clause: «ترجو ...» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كنت.
Clause: «يلقى إليك الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يلقى ...) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, its governing word being ترجو.
Clause: «تكوننّ ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if the Book is cast to you, then do not be a supporter ..."
(87) (الواو) a conjunction (لا) a prohibitive that jusses (يصدّنّك) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn, and the mentioned (النون) is for emphasis and the omitted (الواو), omitted because of the meeting of two sākin letters, is the agent, and (الكاف) is the direct object (عن آيات) attached to (يصدّنّك), (بعد) an accusative adverb attached to (يصدّنّك), (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi, and the deputy agent of the passive verb (أنزلت) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", referring to the verses (إليك) attached to (أنزلت), (الواو) a conjunction (إلى ربّك) attached to (ادع), (لا تكوننّ) like the first (من المشركين) attached to the predicate of تكونّن.
Clause: «لا يصدّنّك ...» is conjoined to the clause لا تكونّن.
Clause: «أنزلت ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «ادع ...» is conjoined to the clause لا يصدّنك ...
Clause: «لا تكونن (the second) ...» is conjoined to the clause لا يصدّنك (88) (الواو) a conjunction (لا) a prohibitive that jusses (مع) an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl of (إلها) , (إلّا) a particle of exception in both places (هو) in the position of a nominative, a badal for the pronoun present in the omitted predicate of لا (وجهه) excepted, accusative (له) attached to an omitted fronted predicate of the subject الحكم (الواو) a conjunction (إليه) attached to the passive (ترجعون), and the (الواو) is the deputy agent.
Clause: «لا تدع ...» is conjoined to the clause لا تكوننّ (the second).
Clause: «لا إله إلّا هو ...» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
Clause: «كلّ شيء هالك ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the preceding prohibitions.
Clause: «له الحكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is a second justification.
Clause: «إليه ترجعون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the justificatory clause.

* Rhetoric:
The free-relation figurative usage (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ:
الوجه ("face") means the essence (dhāt); it is a majāz mursal, and a widespread figure. It may be specific to what is most honoured of essences, and that may be considered here and made the point of the departure from "except Him" to what is in the majestic composition.
